traceability.notes:
The story 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS is fully implemented.
All acceptance criteria are met: - Core Functionality: storyPathPattern and requirementIdPattern (plus corresponding example fields) are implemented in AnnotationRuleOptions, resolved into runtime RegExp and example strings, and consumed by valid-annotation-format. - Backward Compatibility: when no options are supplied or when patterns are invalid, resolvePattern returns the default patterns (getDefaultStoryPattern/getDefaultReqPattern), preserving existing behavior. - Pattern Validation: resolvePattern validates regex sources with try/catch, records configuration errors in optionErrors, and valid-annotation-format.create reports them via invalidRuleConfiguration without crashing. - Error Messages: buildStoryErrorMessage and buildReqErrorMessage use the resolved storyExample/reqExample values, and tests verify that custom and nested examples are reflected in messages. - Quality Standards / Schema: getRuleSchema provides a strict JSON Schema for all options, used as meta.schema for the rule; configuration types and additionalProperties: false align with ESLint best practices. - Integration: valid-annotation-format focuses on format-level validation using configurable patterns while valid-story-reference handles file existence and directories via storyDirectories. The new pattern configuration does not conflict with valid-story-reference, so both rules can be configured together coherently. - Documentation: docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md documents nested and flat options, default behavior, precedence rules, and invalid configuration handling, matching the implementation and tests.
Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts explicitly reference this story and its requirements, cover nested and flat configuration, invalid regex fallback, and example message behavior, and all pass under the Jest run. Therefore this specification is fully satisfied.
